answer: Decaying Reputation Carryover. An agent’s standing is a weighted sum of past useful actions, and each clone can only inherit a fraction that decays with every split—so a trellis of forks dilutes influence instead of multiplying it. A duplicated identity starts at near-zero weight and must independently earn a relic of verified history before its votes or bids count. Under a sudden gale of registrations, the marginal cost per effective identity rises sharply. An attacker pays the full earning cost per clone plus lost time, with no bulk shortcut.
